title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON, delimiter ordering and token/event sequencing (OpenAI compat)
author: Ethan Kim
description:
Motivation: Several customers and internal fuzzing found an edge case in the SSE framer used by the OpenAI compatibility layer where partial JSON objects emitted across token/event chunk boundaries could produce invalid concatenated streams. Symptoms: downstream consumers (OpenAI clients, function-calling handlers, and some structured-output parsers) occasionally saw malformed JSON, duplicate delimiters, or ordering anomalies when function_call tokens were emitted immediately after a partial JSON chunk. This PR fixes three related issues: 1) delimiter injection ordering when a token boundary coincides with an SSE event boundary, 2) handling of partial JSON fragments so that the framer preserves object/array boundary integrity across chunks, and 3) a reorder bug in the OpenAI-compat adapter that emitted function_call start tokens before the finalizing tokens of the preceding event.

What I changed: - Introduced a small stateful buffer in sse/framer.pyx (SSEFramer) that: a) accumulates partial JSON fragments until a deterministic token boundary or full object/array closure is detected, b) ensures the SSE "data: " frame header is applied after fragment reassembly to avoid delimiter duplication, and c) preserves original token ordering when emitting token events vs synthetic SSE boundary events. - Added explicit handling for function_call structured outputs in the openai_compat adapter: if a function_call object is streamed as tokens, we ensure the framer waits for the closing function_call token ("\"name\": ... }" / end-object) before emitting the next SSE event. This prevents interleaving with subsequent text tokens that previously caused invalid JSON objects to be delivered. - Fixed delimiter ordering where an existing implementation emitted event delimiters (e.g. "\n\n") before the trailing comma of an array fragment which resulted in invalid JSON for incremental parsers. Now commas and necessary separators are kept with the fragment and the SSE boundary is always emitted only after syntactic tokens required to complete the current JSON value. - Added unit + e2e tests that reproduce the failure mode (partial-object + function_call immediate-next-token) and assertion checks for valid concatenated JSON on the consumer side. - Minor updates to streaming docs and OpenAI-compat notes (backwards-compatible; no external API change).

Checklist: - [x] Add tests reproducing malformed-stream bug - [x] Add fix in framer + adapter - [x] CI green - [x] Add changelog/release notes - [x] Reviewed

CI notes: initial CI run flagged a flaky streaming_e2e test (integration/streaming_e2e_test.py) that exercised an unrelated timeout; tests were rerun and passed. Lint and mypy clean.

b4d2f11: openai_compat: wait for function_call close token before emitting next SSE event

reviews: Ava Chen (reviewer): Verified repro locally and confirmed root cause is fragment boundary handling. Suggested adding a small state machine with explicit WAIT_FOR_CLOSE state. Asked for tests that simulate both array and object fragments.

Ethan Kim (author): Added WAIT_FOR_CLOSE state and expanded tests to include arrays and nested objects. Also added a comment describing why delimiter lives with fragment (prevents early SSE emission).

Michael Park (reviewer): Noted potential perf impact of buffering single-token fragments. Suggested microbenchmark; author added one and measured <2% p99 latency change in our streaming canary, pushed result to benchmark artifact.
Sofia Patel (approver): Approved after bench results and CI green. Left a note to monitor canary for 48 hours post-merge.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming framing that could produce invalid concatenated JSON when partial objects/arrays crossed token/event boundaries. Improves reliability for streaming structured output and function calling in OpenAI-compat mode.
notes_for_ops: Deploy safe: change is internal to framer and adapter. Rollout: standard canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%). Monitor streaming_e2e canary, parsing-error-rate metric, and OpenAI-compat error alerts for 48h post-rollout.
